claims.text: US President Donald Trump stated that the war against Iran will end immediately after the upcoming US midterm elections.
US President Donald Trump claimed Iran is stalling an end to the war to secure a more favorable political environment in the US ahead of the midterms.
US Energy Secretary Chris Wright stated that the US may continue strikes against Iranian nuclear infrastructure instead of reaching a nuclear deal.
A poll conducted in August 2026 showed that only 31 percent of Americans support the war in Iran, down from 37 percent in March.
The military conflict against Iran was launched on February 28, 2026, by the US and Israel.
Iran stated it attacked 10 ships near the Strait of Hormuz after the US military sank five Iranian oil tankers.
Benchmark Brent crude futures breached $100 a barrel for the first time since July 2026.
One seafarer was killed and another was reported missing aboard the oil products tanker Hercules Star off Dubai following an attack.
The Iranian Revolutionary Guards stated they would hit 20 targets if their enemy struck two or three targets.
US President Donald Trump stated that the US military has knocked out about nine Iranian oil tankers.
The Dutch benchmark gas contract rose by almost 4% to €78.73 a megawatt hour, reaching its highest level since January 2023.
China's crude oil imports recovered to nearly 9 million barrels per day in August 2026, up from 7.15 million in June.
US Central Command stated its strikes destroyed four Iranian tankers in the Gulf of Oman—Kaviz, Charminar, Horizon 1, and Riesco—and a fifth tanker, Derya, near Kharg Island.
Jordan's armed forces reported intercepting 20 Iranian missiles aimed at Muwaffaq Salti Air Base, with no casualties reported.
IRGC spokesman Hossein Mohebi announced plans to set coordinates for a new prohibited zone covering parts of the Sea of Oman and the Arabian Sea.
Apple unveiled its first foldable smartphone, named the iPhone Duo, starting at a price of $1,999.
The iPhone Duo opens into a horizontal 7.6-inch-wide screen.
Apple announced that pre-orders for the iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max begin on September 12, 2026, with store availability starting September 18, 2026.
Apple raised the base price of the standard iPhone 17 in India from Rs 82,900 to Rs 99,900.
Apple increased the retail price of the ultra-thin iPhone Air in India by Rs 30,000, bringing it to Rs 1,49,900.
Apple made the iPhone Duo an eSIM-only device globally by completely eliminating the physical SIM tray.
Apple claims the iPhone Duo delivers up to 31 hours of video playback on its inner display and up to 44 hours on its outer display.
The iPhone Duo omits Face ID in favor of a Touch ID sensor embedded in the power button to save internal space.
Apple introduced the Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4, both equipped with the new S11 processor.
Apple introduced native 'Readiness score' daily tracking across its new smartwatches.
In India, the iPhone 18 Pro starts at Rs 1,64,900, while the iPhone 18 Pro Max starts at Rs 1,79,900.
The iPhone 18 Pro lineup introduces Apple Reference Image, a feature that uses signed sensor data to verify photo authenticity.
The iPhone 18 Pro series is powered by Apple's A20 Pro processor built on 2-nanometer technology.
In India, the iPhone Duo starts at Rs 2,99,900 for the 256GB model and ranges up to Rs 4,49,900 for the 2TB model.
The IAEA Board of Governors passed a resolution reporting Iran to the UN Security Council for non-compliance with its non-proliferation obligations.
Twenty-three countries voted in favor of the IAEA resolution reporting Iran, while Russia, China, and Niger voted against it.
Wednesday's resolution by the 35-member IAEA board is the first time in 20 years that Iran has been reported to the UN Security Council.
The IAEA suspects Iran holds approximately 400kg of highly enriched uranium, sufficient to potentially produce 10 nuclear weapons if further enriched.
Iran's mission to the UN stated that the nuclear non-compliance situation was created solely because of criminal acts of aggression by the US and Israel.
The IAEA resolution against Iran was submitted jointly by the United Kingdom, France, Germany, and the United States.
Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi stated that US and Israeli attacks disrupted nuclear inspections and were then used as a pretext to pass an IAEA resolution.
Senior US officials stated that Iran possessed roughly 440kg of 60% enriched uranium at the start of the latest conflict.
China, Russia, and Iran rejected the legal basis of the IAEA vote, arguing that reporting Iran risks politicizing a technical matter.
Iran circulated an 11-page diplomatic document warning Western nations against converting the IAEA into a tool of war.
US President Donald Trump stated on September 4 that the US may soon hit the Pickaxe facility south of Natanz.
UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham defended a trade ban on products from Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank.
UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband announced sweeping UK sanctions on trade with Israeli settlements in the West Bank.
UK Chief Rabbi Sir Ephraim Mirvis condemned the UK settlement sanctions, describing the decision as a 'dark day for British Jews'.
Prominent British rabbis, including Masorti Rabbi Jonathan Wittenberg and Liberal Rabbi Alexandra Wright, publicly voiced support for the UK settlement sanctions.
Twelve countries, including Britain, France, and Canada, coordinated to sanction trade with Israeli settlements in the West Bank.
Former Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Olmert and former military chief Dan Halutz signed a joint statement welcoming the UK sanctions on settlements.
Exports from occupied territories to the UK totaled $45 million last year out of $4.4 billion in total trade between the UK and Israel.
A poll by the Jewish People Policy Institute found that nearly three-quarters of Jewish Israelis support partial or total annexation of the occupied West Bank.
UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband stated that Israeli intelligence gave assurances that intelligence sharing with the UK will continue unchanged despite the trade sanctions.
US President Donald Trump stated he would speak to Israel to find out their thinking regarding the settlement sanctions imposed by allied nations.
The UK government announced fresh nuclear-related sanctions targeting Iranian ships involved in malign behavior.
Republican National Committee Chair Joe Gruters opened the two-day Republican midterm convention at the American Airlines Center in Dallas, Texas.
The pro-Trump Super PAC Maga Inc holds a $400 million war chest and earmarked $47 million for seven competitive midterm races.
Challengers of Missouri's congressional redistricting map filed an emergency appeal with the US Supreme Court after a federal judge ordered Missouri to use a new Republican-drawn map in the midterms.
An emergency inflatable slide on Air Force One was accidentally deployed prior to Donald Trump's departure to Dallas.
The gathering at the American Airlines Center in Dallas is the first midterm convention held by the Republican Party.
A Reuters/Ipsos poll showed US President Donald Trump with an approval rating of 33 percent.
An FT/Focaldata poll indicated that 57 percent of respondents believe their personal financial situation has worsened since Donald Trump re-took office.
The 109-item schedule for the Republican convention includes a segment on the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 attacks but excludes any segment on the ongoing war with Iran.
Republicans organized the midterm convention in Dallas with US President Donald Trump slated as the primary keynote speaker for both nights.
The far-right Alternative für Deutschland (AfD) won 43.8% of the vote in the Saxony-Anhalt state election on September 6.
The Christian Democratic Union (CDU) vote share in Saxony-Anhalt fell to 17.2%, down from 37.1% in 2021.
Voter turnout in the Saxony-Anhalt state election reached nearly 78%.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz cancelled a planned telephone call with US President Donald Trump after Trump publicly praised the AfD's state election victory.
US President Donald Trump posted on Truth Social celebrating the AfD's election victory and ended his statement with 'MGGA!!!'.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz accused the AfD of seeking 'ethnic cleansing' during a Bundestag parliamentary debate.
Serbian President Aleksandar Vučić dissolved parliament and announced snap elections for October 2026.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz stated in parliament that one in six skilled workers in Germany has a migration background.
Bundestag President Julia Klöckner threatened to expel shouting AfD lawmakers from the chamber during the parliamentary debate.
AfD co-leader Alice Weidel told the Bundestag that Friedrich Merz's coalition was a failure and that his time as chancellor was up.
The AfD won nearly 44% of the vote in Saxony-Anhalt but fell three seats short of an absolute majority.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz criticized the AfD for failing to condemn a drone bomb attack at Leipzig airport that German intelligence linked to Russia.
